topicName: Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) and Redo Log Internals
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) and Redo Log Internals in MySQL"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"MySQL InnoDB storage engine uses Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) to ensure durability and high performance. The core concept behind WAL is that modifications to data pages must be recorded in stable storage on disk before the actual data pages themselves are written to disk."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"The Architecture of InnoDB Redo Logs"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"The redo log consists of memory buffers known as the log buffer and physical files on disk known as ib_logfile0, ib_logfile1, etc. When DML operations occur, changes are first written to the log buffer in memory and later flushed to the redo log files."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Log Buffer: A memory area that holds data to be written to the log files on disk."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Log Files: Circularly written disk files that store low-level physical changes made to database pages."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"LSN (Log Sequence Number): A continuously growing 8-byte integer that tracks the byte offset in the redo log stream."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Configuring Redo Log Parameters"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"MySQL provides parameters to tune the redo log size and flush behavior to balance performance against crash recovery time. You can view these configurations using SQL statements."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'innodb_log_%';"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding innodb_flush_log_at_trx_commit"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"The variable innodb_flush_log_at_trx_commit controls how the log buffer is written to disk during a transaction commit, significantly impacting durability."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Setting 0: The log buffer is written to the log file and flushed to disk once per second. Transactions can be lost in a crash."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Setting 1 (Default): The log buffer is written and flushed to disk at every transaction commit. Maximum durability."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Setting 2: The log buffer is written to the file at every commit, but flushed to disk once per second. High performance with a small risk of loss."},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Crash Recovery Process"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"During startup after a crash, InnoDB compares the LSN found in the data page headers (Checkpoint LSN) with the latest LSN in the redo log. Any changes present in the redo log that have not been flushed to the data files are reapplied. This phase is known as rolling forward."},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"SELECT * FROM performance_schema.global_status WHERE VARIABLE_NAME LIKE 'Innodb_os_log_written';"}]
